# Story 109 — Reports show the reader's day in their own zone (Story: CRM-131)

## Plan review — read this before the sections below

Reviewed 2026-09-02 against the code, every citation opened. Reading the zone
from the runtime rather than guessing it from the language is right, the `UTC`
fallback is right (and works, because `REPORTS-4-API` was made to accept `UTC`
after finding `Intl.supportedValuesOf` omits it), and refusing to do day-boundary
maths on the client is right. **Seven things are wrong.** Where a section below
contradicts this one, this one wins.

### 1 — Agent load has no window, and giving it a period label would make it lie.

The plan sends `timeZone` and `from`/`to` to `/reports/agent-load`, adds a
`window` field to `LoadReport`, renders the period sentence above its figures,
and puts a period switch on the page.

That report deliberately takes no window and its response carries none —
`REPORTS-4-API`'s criteria were amended to say so, because load means *work
still on the person* and a day filter would report an agent holding five
week-old tickets as idle.

A period sentence over it is worse than a wrong number: the numbers would be
right and the label above them would say they are about Tuesday. **Agent load
gets no switch and no period sentence.** It gets one muted line saying it is
what is on the desk now, because an admin who sees a period control on two
report screens and not the third will otherwise wonder whether the third is
broken.

### 2 — The `window` block's shape is invented.

Plan: `{ start: string; end: string; timeZone: string }`. What the API sends:

```json
{ "timeZone": "Africa/Cairo", "from": "2026-09-03", "to": "2026-09-03",
  "startUtc": "2026-09-02T21:00:00.000Z", "endUtc": "2026-09-03T21:00:00.000Z" }
```

or `null` when no window was asked for — which is the ordinary first load, and
the plan has no branch for it.

### 3 — The period label must be read from the answer, not from what was asked.

The plan builds the sentence from client state: `period`, plus `new Date()` for
the "today" case.

The API **echoes the window it used**, and that is not decoration — it is there
so the label and the numbers have one source. Building the label from the
request puts them back on two, and reintroduces exactly what the criterion
forbids: *"a stale number is never shown under a new label."* With the label
coming from client state and the numbers from the response, a slow request
leaves last period's numbers under this period's label — which is the failure,
inverted, and harder to see.

It also removes the `new Date()` problem entirely. "Today" is whichever day the
**API** decided, from its clock; the browser's is a different clock, and on a
desk where the two differ the label would name a day the numbers are not about.

So: render the sentence from `report.window`, and render nothing when it is
null. The `noon UTC` parsing trick in task 3 then has nothing left to solve —
`startUtc` and `endUtc` are real instants and `formatDate` takes them directly.

### 4 — `useRequest` exports `reset`. The plan guesses three ways around it.

Task 4 says: *"Use `useRequest`'s existing `reset` if it exposes one; if not,
add a tiny local `useEffect`… or clears via `run(() => Promise.reject(...))`…
wrap the returned `report` in a `useMemo`… if `useRequest` cannot expose that
seam cleanly…"* — in one paragraph, about a file the plan cites at Context
item 4.

It does export `reset` (`useRequest.ts:44-49`), documented, and
`useCreateAccount` already uses it.

And none of that machinery is needed for the criterion anyway. Task 5 step 8
already solves it: dropping `&& !page` from the loading condition shows the
skeleton whenever a request is in flight, because `run` sets `status` to
`'loading'` on every call. The numbers and the label then change together
because both come from the same response (item 3).

### 5 — `t.reports.period.today` is three levels deep, and there is no `reports` group.

The dictionary is a top-level group of string leaves, and the groups these three
pages use are `queueReport`, `promiseReport` and `agentLoadReport` — not
`queueByStatusReport` / `promiseShareReport` as the plan names them twice.

One new top-level group, `reportPeriod`, with flat leaves — shared by the two
screens that have a period, which is what the plan's "no per-report
duplication" note is reaching for.

### 6 — `t.errors.UNPROCESSABLE` does not exist.

The code is **`VALIDATION_FAILED`** — `errors.js:18`, mirrored in
`web/src/shared/api/errors.ts`. `t.errors` is
`satisfies Record<ApiErrorCode, string>`, so the name in the plan would not
compile, which is the guard working.

### 7 — The presets are fine; the ranges are worth stating.

`last7` as a 6-day-back inclusive span and `last30` as 29 are both correct
readings of "the last seven days" including today. Keep them, and say so in the
code — the off-by-one is the kind of thing a later reader silently "fixes".

## Story Goal

An admin who opens any of the three reports sees numbers stamped with the period they cover, in **their** locale, computed against **their** browser's IANA zone (not UTC, not a language guess). When the reader picks a different preset period, the request is re-sent with the same zone, the previous numbers are cleared before the new ones land, and the sentence describing the period changes together with the numbers — never one under the label of the other.

Out of scope (do **not** implement):
- No zone picker (the browser owns the zone).
- No client-side day-boundary math (the client sends the zone; the API decides the rows).
- No calendar widget, no date library, no free-form date range input.
- No API changes.

---

- **L-63 — Don't fire a request the caller knows will be refused.** Existing `enabled` guard is kept.

## Frontend Tasks

`No backend changes required.` CRM-130 already delivered the API surface.

### 1 — Read the reader's IANA zone from the runtime

**Create file:** `web/src/pages/reports/reader-zone.ts`

```ts
// The reader's IANA zone as the runtime knows it. Not a constant, not a guess
// from language — Arabic does not mean Cairo. When the runtime refuses to name
// a zone (very old engine, hardened environment), fall back to 'UTC' so the
// API still gets a valid value and answers, rather than 422-ing the page.
export function readerZone(): string {
  try {
    const zone = Intl.DateTimeFormat().resolvedOptions().timeZone;
    return zone && zone.length > 0 ? zone : 'UTC';
  } catch {
    return 'UTC';
  }
}
```

Add a single unit test `web/src/pages/reports/reader-zone.test.ts` that mocks `Intl.DateTimeFormat` to return `''` and asserts the fallback is `'UTC'`, and one that spies on the real value and asserts a non-empty string.

### 2 — Period presets shared by the three reports

**Create file:** `web/src/pages/reports/report-period.ts`

```ts
// Preset periods the report screens offer. No calendar, no date library.
// 'today' sends no from/to — the API defaults to the reader's local today.
// The other two send YYYY-MM-DD strings built from the reader's zone via
// Intl.DateTimeFormat with { timeZone, year, month, day } — no client-side
// midnight math (out of scope).
export type PeriodKey = 'today' | 'last7' | 'last30';

export type Period = {
  key: PeriodKey;
  from?: string; // YYYY-MM-DD, reader's zone
  to?: string;   // YYYY-MM-DD, reader's zone (inclusive; API is [from, to])
};

export function buildPeriod(key: PeriodKey, timeZone: string, nowMs = Date.now()): Period {
  if (key === 'today') return { key };
  const days = key === 'last7' ? 6 : 29; // inclusive window
  const to = ymdInZone(nowMs, timeZone);
  const from = ymdInZone(nowMs - days * 86_400_000, timeZone);
  return { key, from, to };
}

function ymdInZone(ms: number, timeZone: string): string {
  // en-CA is YYYY-MM-DD by design.
  return new Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-CA', {
    timeZone, year: 'numeric', month: '2-digit', day: '2-digit',
  }).format(new Date(ms));
}

export function periodQuery(p: Period, timeZone: string): string {
  const params = new URLSearchParams({ timeZone });
  if (p.from) params.set('from', p.from);
  if (p.to) params.set('to', p.to);
  return `?${params.toString()}`;
}
```

Add `report-period.test.ts` covering: `today` produces no `from`/`to`; `last7` and `last30` produce `from` and `to` that are the correct number of days apart; `periodQuery` always includes `timeZone`; unknown zones are passed through untouched (validation is the API's job).

## Edge Cases & Failure Modes

- **`Intl.DateTimeFormat().resolvedOptions().timeZone` returns empty string.** Fallback is `'UTC'`. Enforced in `reader-zone.ts` (see § 1).
- **API returns `422 { fields: ['timeZone'] }` because the runtime named a zone the server does not know.** The existing `ErrorState` branch renders `t.errors.UNPROCESSABLE`; no special case. `readerZone`'s `'UTC'` fallback covers the "no zone at all" path.
- **Reader picks `last7`, then quickly picks `last30` before the first request lands.** `useRequest` fires the second request; the stale-guard (§ 4) clears the returned `report` on period change, so the screen shows the skeleton, not the `last7` numbers under a `last30` label.
- **Language switch mid-page.** The period sentence re-renders from `t` and the `formatDate` output changes locale; the underlying request is unchanged (locale is not zone).
- **DST boundary during the reader's session.** `readerZone` is memoised per mount, so a session that crosses DST keeps the same zone id; behaviour matches the API's day-boundary math (which uses the zone id, not the offset). Documented in a comment beside `useMemo` in each page.
- **Non-admin arrives at the route.** `isAdmin === false` still returns the `EmptyState`; the hook is `enabled: false`, so no request is made (L-63).
- **Zone id contains RTL-neutral characters** (`Africa/Cairo`, `America/New_York`). The zone is rendered inside `<Isolated>` so bidi wrapping keeps it intact in Arabic layout.

## Migration / Rollback

- Pure additive on the wire: the API accepts the new params today and returns `window` today (CRM-130 shipped). No feature flag, no data migration.
- **Rollback:** revert this story's commits. Reports revert to the pre-CRM-130 behaviour (no `timeZone`, no `window` in the UI) — the API stays backwards-compatible because `timeZone` is optional.
- **Half-applied risk:** if the i18n keys ship without the page code (or vice-versa), `parity.test.ts` and `no-hardcoded-strings.test.ts` will fail before merge. Do not split the changes across PRs.

## Done Criteria

- [x] The zone is read from the runtime — `Intl.DateTimeFormat().resolvedOptions().timeZone` — never guessed from the language. Arabic does not mean Cairo.
- [x] A runtime that will not name a zone gets `UTC`, which is a real answer rather than a refusal: the API accepts it, so the report still answers and the label says which day it is about.
- [x] **"Everything" is the default** and asks with no zone at all. Defaulting to today would have quietly turned "the queue by status" into "raised today, by status" — the same numbers, the same page, a different question. It is also the exact request every caller written before the window existed made.
- [x] Choosing a period sends the reader's zone and, for the two ranges, the dates in that zone.
- [x] **The label is read from the window the API echoed**, never from what the client asked for (review item 3). One source, so the period and the numbers cannot disagree — and "today" is whichever day the API's clock decided, not the browser's.
- [x] The label's dates are formatted **in the report's zone**, not the browser's. Found by a test: a Cairo window starts at 21:00Z the day before, so the browser's zone often names the wrong day outright, three words from a sentence saying which zone it was read in.
- [x] A range names its last day, not the instant after it — the window's end is the start of the day following the last one included.
- [x] **A number is never left under a period it does not belong to.** The figures are hidden while a request is in flight, not merely covered by a skeleton (see below).
- [x] **Agent load gets no period control and no period sentence** (review item 1), and one muted line saying it is what is on the desk now — so an admin who sees a control on the other two does not wonder whether this one is broken.
- [x] Dates and the zone id are isolate-wrapped (L-51); a zone id is a left-to-right run with a slash in it.
- [x] Flat i18n leaves in one `reportPeriod` group, shared by the two screens that have a period.
- [x] `cd web && npm run build` clean; `npm test` — 400 pass. `cd api && npm test` — 617 pass. Six guards green.
- [x] No AI-attribution strings in the diff.

## What the mutation pass proved, and what the tests found first

| # | what was broken | result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| V1 | stale figures stay under the new label | 1 fail |
| V2 | "everything" asks with a zone anyway | 3 fail |
| V3 | the inclusive span is off by one | 2 fail |
| V4 | the label is formatted in the browser's zone | 1 fail |
| V5 | the range names the instant after its last day | 1 fail |

**V1 is a correction to this review.** Item 4 said dropping `&& !page` from the
loading condition "already solves it". It does not: `useRequest` keeps the last
answer while the next request is in flight, so the skeleton appeared **and** the
previous period's figures stayed underneath it — which looks like a screen
loading more rather than one showing the wrong thing. The content branch had to
be gated too. The test found it; the review had said the opposite.

**V4 is a defect the test found before any mutation.** The label formatted its
dates with the browser's zone while the sentence beside it named the report's.
On this machine the two happen to agree, so the first version of that test
passed for the wrong reason; it was rewritten around a New York window, where
they differ.
